# Riverside Annex Shuttle Protocol

Fictional evaluation document. Scope: transport administration for the 2027 policy year. Effective dates are supplied separately in the corpus manifest. This document must be read alongside other selected sources when the question names another office or location.

## Booking cutoff

Riverside Annex shuttle seats must be reserved by 12:00 two business days before travel.

Transport reservations are administered separately from lesson attendance. A vacant classroom place does not establish a vacant shuttle seat. A responsible adult must confirm the correct campus, travel date, and collection arrangement. For this section the desk records the request under TRANSPORT-2027-01. The reference groups correspondence; it does not change the deadline or amount stated above. A correction must preserve the original entry and record the reason for the change.

## Working example: booking cutoff

Consider a case where a dancer changes the travel booking while keeping the dance lesson. The immediate question concerns booking cutoff, not every rule in the transport file. The administrator checks route manifests, collection points, and transport credits before replying. A common error is that a family reads the Main Campus cutoff while booking an Annex departure. Read the named source and policy year before treating a nearby number as the answer. Record which document supported the explanation so that another staff member can reproduce the check. If the request also mentions a different service, preserve it as a separate issue instead of assuming that one approval covers both activities.

## Cross-service boundary

This transport document does not grant authority over unrelated activities. A staff member should distinguish the stated rule from a future booking, payment, or discretionary approval. A family may ask several questions in one message; answerable portions should cite the relevant source while missing facts remain unresolved. An unanswered detail must not be inferred from an adjacent fee, deadline, room number, or event identifier. In particular, general guidance about route manifests, collection points, and transport credits is not a substitute for an explicit rule about a different programme.

## Handling incomplete requests

When a transport request omits the student, location, policy year, or relevant date, the desk records the missing information and asks for it. The original wording is preserved in the working notes. Staff avoid copying identity documents into teaching chat or broad distribution lists. A later clarification supplements rather than overwrites the request. This distinction matters when a dancer changes the travel booking while keeping the dance lesson. A response acknowledging receipt is administrative correspondence and should not be represented as approval of an exception.

## Audit example and non-equivalence

The reviewer reconstructs the event from route manifests, collection points, and transport credits. For example, an entered reference code may identify correspondence without proving that money moved, a class place was reserved, or a consent decision changed. The reviewer compares the dated source with the actual record and records unresolved inconsistencies. Similar words across offices are not proof of identical policies: deposit, credit, submission, and acknowledgement each have a specific role in their own service. The desk retains source identity rather than combining conflicting numbers into a new undocumented rule.

## Final journey check

After the final Riverside Annex shuttle stop, the escort must call dispatch before leaving the vehicle.

This is the last substantive instruction in this source. The closing check must be performed after the ordinary service tasks, not inferred from an earlier example. If the closing check cannot be verified, mark the item unresolved rather than copying a previous day’s completion status. End of policy text.
